title: Appliance Pair (In-Path) Health and Redundancy
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Appliance Pair (In-Path) Health and Redundancy' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_appliance_pair_in_path_health_and_redundancy` (UC-5.16.5), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Appliance Pair (In-Path) Health and Redundancy", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=wanop` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' that satisfy the UC-5.16.5 SPL filters for 'Appliance Pair (In-Path) Health and Redundancy'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `wanop` / `target_sourcetype` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `operational_exceptions.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-5.16.5.

dataSources: Detailed: `index=wanop OR index=network`; HA heartbeat syslog (`riverbed:steelhead` neighbor failover lines), EdgeConnect Orchestrator cluster telemetry (`silverpeak:*`), Citrix SD-WAN HA/control-plane transitions (`citrix:sdwan*`), supplemental ICMP/path probes mirrored beside ZDX when correlating SaaS exits. Fields such as `ha_role`, `cluster_state`, `serial`, `inpath_mode`, `alarm_level` feed pairwise pivots. Collected via Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Vendor syslog/TAs, optional Splunk Synthetic Monitoring pings bridged via HTTP Event Collector for tertiary witnesses. — Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833)
spl:
index=wanop OR index=network earliest=-8h
| eval v=lower(sourcetype)
| eval vendor=case(match(v,"riverbed|steelhead"),"Riverbed SteelHead",match(v,"silverpeak|edgeconnect"),"Silver Peak EdgeConnect",match(v,"citrix"),"Citrix SD-WAN WANOP",match(v,"zdx|zscaler"),"Zscaler Digital Experience","other")
| where vendor!="other"
| eval pair=coalesce(ha_group,inpath_pair_id,cluster_name,deployment_site,"singleton")
| eval healthy=case(match(lower(coalesce(alarm_level,severity,"")),"critical|major|down|failed"),0,match(lower(coalesce(appliance_state,health_status,opt_status,"")),"online|up|ok|healthy|nominal"),1,isnull(appliance_state) AND NOT match(_raw,"(?i)(failover|down|offline|lost peer)"),1,0)
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(eval(if(healthy=1,host,null()))) as healthy_appliances dc(host) as total_seen values(appliance_state) as states max(eval(if(healthy=0,1,0))) as fault_seen by pair vendor _time
| eval quorum_ratio=if(total_seen>0, round(healthy_appliances/total_seen,3), null())
| where total_seen>0 AND healthy_appliances<total_seen
| stats latest(quorum_ratio) as quorum latest(healthy_appliances) as healthy latest(total_seen) as declared_members latest(states) as raw_states by pair vendor
| sort quorum vendor pair
description: Quarter-hour Splunk bucketing counts healthy appliances sharing identical HA pair identifiers so asymmetric failover—only one surviving member online—or oscillating cluster partitions triggers paging ahead of black-holed WAN segments.
value: Branch resilience audits rely on automated quorum telemetry rather than quarterly manual CLI snapshots while auditors prove redundancy commitments during SOC exercises referencing Splunk-backed timelines.
implementation: Map orchestrator exports into deterministic `pair` keys, mute transient flap alerts using `streamstats` requiring three consecutive failing buckets.
visualization: Chord diagram optional; pragmatic cluster matrix listing pair vs quorum_ratio plus sparkline from stacked stats.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance** — Planned change generates expected deviations for 'Appliance Pair (In-Path) Health and Redundancy'. Cross-check change records.

2. **Batch job cycle** — Fixed-schedule workload skews `wanop` metrics.

3. **Monitoring synthetic checks** — Health probes from known hosts.

4. **Onboarding burst** — New entities produce atypical volume until baseline stabilizes.

**Suppression mechanism:** `operational_exceptions.csv` with entity, reason, valid_until.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• CMDB linking serial numbers to street addresses for notification routing.
• Clarified naming scheme so active/standby pairs share identical `pair` tokens.
• Maintenance playbook referencing bypass cabling steps when hardware fails.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ensure failover syslog severity retained even during floods; configure persistence queues on forwarders.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Save SPL as `wanopt_ha_pair_gap`; alert when `healthy_appliances==1 AND total_seen>=2` for thirty minutes.

Step 3 — Validate
Fail lab secondary intentionally—confirm Splunk transitions align with optical bypass LED patterns.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Glass-table style dashboard overlays vendor icons with pair clusters and embedded runbook URLs.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
**Split-brain:** totals mismatch across syslog duplicates—dedupe by serial.**Cloud-managed EdgeConnect:** aggregator delay—extend `_time` tolerance.**ZDX-only witnesses:** do not infer hardware HA solely from cloud probes.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Vendor syslog/TAs, optional Splunk Synthetic Monitoring pings bridged via HTTP Event Collector for tertiary witnesses. — Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into wanop, network. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time, healthy, pair, quorum_ratio`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Most offices have two boxes backing each other up so the internet helper keeps working if one gets sick. We compare notes from both boxes so we notice when only half the team is left standing.
